subject: science
title: Rocks
description: Comparing and grouping rocks by their appearance and properties, how fossils are formed, and how soil is made from rocks and organic matter.

objectives.statement: Compare and group together different kinds of rocks on the basis of their appearance and simple physical properties.
Describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock.
Recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter.

questions.ask: Name one property you could use to compare two rocks.
questions.claim: One property you could use to compare two rocks is {}.
questions.answer: hardness

questions.ask: A rock that lets water soak into it is described as...
questions.claim: A rock that lets water soak into it is described as {}.
questions.answer: permeable

questions.ask: Which is harder: granite, or chalk?
questions.claim: {} is harder than chalk.
questions.answer: granite

questions.ask: Which rock would be better for building a house: a hard rock like granite, or a soft, crumbly rock like chalk?
questions.claim: {} would be better for building a house than a soft, crumbly rock like chalk.
questions.answer: a hard rock like granite
distractors: a soft, crumbly rock like chalk

questions.ask: To test which of two rocks is harder, you could...
questions.claim: To test which of two rocks is harder, you could {}.
questions.answer: see which one scratches the other

questions.ask: Why is a hard, waterproof rock like granite good for building?
questions.claim: Granite is good for building because {}.
questions.answer: it is strong and does not let water soak in
acceptableAnswers: it is hard and lasts a long time
distractors: it is very light and floats

questions.ask: Chalk is a soft rock. What happens if you rub it along the ground?
questions.claim: If you rub chalk along the ground, {}.
questions.answer: it leaves a mark and wears away

questions.ask: What is a fossil?
questions.claim: A fossil is {}.
questions.answer: the preserved remains of an ancient living thing, found in rock
acceptableAnswers: the remains of a dead animal or plant in rock
the shape of an old living thing in rock

questions.ask: What are fossils usually found inside?
questions.claim: Fossils are usually found inside {}.
questions.answer: rock

questions.ask: What best describes how a fossil forms?
questions.claim: A fossil forms when {}.
questions.answer: an animal is trapped in rock and its shape is preserved over a very long time
distractors: an animal turns to stone in a few days
a rock grows legs and moves
a plant is painted onto a rock
an animal turns to gold instantly
a fossil is carved by a person

questions.ask: What can fossils teach us about?
questions.claim: Fossils can teach us about {}.
questions.answer: animals and plants that lived millions of years ago

questions.ask: Do fossils form very quickly, in a few hours, or very slowly, over millions of years?
questions.claim: Fossils form {}.
questions.answer: very slowly, over millions of years
distractors: very quickly, in a few hours

questions.ask: What is the name of a scientist who studies fossils?
questions.claim: A scientist who studies fossils is called {}.
questions.answer: a palaeontologist

questions.ask: Which part of an animal is most likely to become a fossil?
questions.claim: The part of an animal most likely to become a fossil is {}.
questions.answer: its hard bones or shell

questions.ask: What are soils made from?
questions.claim: Soils are made from {}.
questions.answer: broken rock and organic matter
acceptableAnswers: broken up rock and rotted plants
distractors: sand from a beach shop only

questions.ask: What is the name for the rotted plant and animal material found in soil?
questions.claim: The rotted plant and animal material found in soil is called {}.
questions.answer: organic matter

questions.ask: Where do the tiny pieces of rock in soil come from?
questions.claim: The tiny pieces of rock in soil come from {}.
questions.answer: larger rocks broken down over a long time
distractors: they fall from the sky as rain

questions.ask: As well as organic matter, what else does soil contain?
questions.claim: As well as organic matter, soil also contains {}.
questions.answer: pieces of broken-down rock

questions.ask: Is soil actually made from only water, or from a mixture of broken rock and organic matter?
questions.claim: Soil is actually made from {}.
questions.answer: a mixture of broken rock and organic matter

questions.ask: Why is soil important for plants?
questions.claim: Soil is important for plants because {}.
questions.answer: it gives their roots somewhere to grow and holds water and nutrients
distractors: plants do not need soil for anything
